list.description: The scrape job to look at: one job is one network. Single-select on purpose — chain-level panels sum seqnos, block rates and collation budgets across whatever the selector spans, so a multi-job selection would merge unrelated fleets (mainnet + testnet) into one meaningless chain. Compare networks in two tabs.

list.description: Node filter within the selected job. Node and fleet-diagnostic panels respect it; chain-truth panels explicitly query every reporter in the job so selecting one node cannot redefine the blockchain.

panels.description: One row per selected hero, sorted by hidden severity. Red means the target or rebroadcaster is down, the older candidate/finality stream for either chain has been silent for more than 15 seconds, or a validated external had no protected route in the last five minutes. Yellow starts at five seconds of broadcast silence.

panels.title: Master candidate broadcast source
panels.description: Share of selected master candidate broadcasts by the source whose first arrival won rebroadcast deduplication over the visible time range.

panels.title: Master finality broadcast source
panels.description: Share of selected master finality broadcasts by the source whose first arrival won rebroadcast deduplication over the visible time range.

panels.title: Shard candidate broadcast source
panels.description: Share of selected shard candidate broadcasts by the source whose first arrival won rebroadcast deduplication over the visible time range.

panels.title: Shard finality broadcast source
panels.description: Share of selected shard finality broadcasts by the source whose first arrival won rebroadcast deduplication over the visible time range.

panels.title: Master broadcast rate by hero
panels.description: Master candidate and finality broadcasts/s scheduled from protected or custom overlays to the public Plumtree overlay by each selected hero. Candidate and finality totals separately sum their first-arrival sources.

panels.title: Shard broadcast rate by hero
panels.description: Shard candidate and finality broadcasts/s scheduled from protected or custom overlays to the public Plumtree overlay by each selected hero. Candidate and finality totals separately sum their first-arrival sources.

panels.title: Master arrival rate by hero
panels.description: Master candidate and finality arrivals/s received from protected and custom overlays by each selected hero, including arrivals suppressed by rebroadcast deduplication.

panels.title: Shard arrival rate by hero
panels.description: Shard candidate and finality arrivals/s received from protected and custom overlays by each selected hero, including arrivals suppressed by rebroadcast deduplication.

panels.title: Master time since last broadcast
panels.description: Age at scrape time of each selected hero's latest forwarded master candidate and finality. Yellow at 5 seconds and red at 15 seconds. Exporter reachability is monitored separately.

panels.title: Shard time since last broadcast
panels.description: Age at scrape time of each selected hero's latest forwarded shard candidate and finality. Yellow at 5 seconds and red at 15 seconds. Exporter reachability is monitored separately.

panels.title: Master Plumtree eager peers by hero
panels.description: Average eager-set size across the master public overlay's Plumtree broadcast trees. Eager peers receive full candidate/finality payloads; the rest receive IHAVEs.

panels.title: Shard Plumtree eager peers by hero
panels.description: Average eager-set size across the shard public overlay's Plumtree broadcast trees. Eager peers receive full candidate/finality payloads; the rest receive IHAVEs.

panels.title: Public overlay peers by hero
panels.description: Current public-overlay peer-table size for every selected hero and chain. The separate eager-peer panels show the peers currently receiving full Plumtree payloads.

panels.title: External relay outcomes by hero
panels.description: Validated public external messages/s reaching the relay stage. Relayed means the message was submitted to the matching protected overlay; no_protected_route means no matching overlay was available and the message was dropped.
